title: Domestication of the dromedary
summary: Excavations at Tell Abraq and Muweilah near Sharjah in the UAE revealed some of the first clear signs of camel domestication, with settlement expansion at both sites around 1000 BCE linked to it. A Bryn Mawr College report says south-eastern Arabia, now the UAE and Oman, was likely where the dromedary was first domesticated.

uncertainty.note: Sources give "around 1000 B.C.E." and "3,000-year-old evidence"; no precise first date is stated.
